A SIMPLE SETUP

Your Watch.
Your equipment.
Your workout.

BikeTrack connects directly from Apple Watch to compatible Bluetooth bikes and treadmills.

FTMSCycling PowerSpeed & Cadence
What do I need?+

An Apple Watch running watchOS 11 or later. For equipment metrics, you’ll need a bike or treadmill that broadcasts a supported standard Bluetooth service.

Will it work with my indoor bike?+

BikeTrack supports standard FTMS Indoor Bike Data, Cycling Power, and Cycling Speed & Cadence. Available metrics depend on your equipment. Specific models have not yet been physically verified, so model compatibility isn’t guaranteed.

Can I record runs and walks, too?+

Yes. Record indoor cycling, running, and walking. Compatible treadmills must broadcast standard FTMS Treadmill Data. You can also record without equipment using measurements from your Watch.

Do I need an account or subscription?+

No. BikeTrack has no account, subscription, advertising, or analytics SDK. Workout data stays in local app storage and Apple Health, subject to your Apple settings.

Does it control resistance or sync to Strava?+

BikeTrack reads your equipment’s metrics; it doesn’t control resistance or ERG mode. Direct Strava export and ANT+ aren’t included. It connects to one Bluetooth peripheral at a time.
